newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania president bows to right's wishes on PM.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania president bows to right's wishes on PM.

text.p: Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas on Thursday bowed to the wishes of the resurgent right-wing and said he would ask its chosen candidate to be prime minister, the domestic news agency ELTA said.

Vytautas Landsbergis, who spearheads the right and led Lithuania's bid for independence from the former Soviet Union in 1990-91, met Brazauskas on Thursday to propose Gediminas Vagnorius as prime minister.
The right scored a landslide victory in elections, ousting the former Communists.
"With such a parliamentary majority, there is no possibility to look for any other options on the issue of nominating the prime minister," Brazauskas was quoted by ELTA as saying.
Landsbergis is expected to become parliamentary speaker and take on Brazauskas for the presidency in 1998.
Landsbergis' Homeland Union party won 70 seats in the elections and is to form a coalition with the Christian Democrats for 86 seats in the 141-seat parliament.
Vagnorius, a bespectacled economist, was prime minister under Landsbergis between 1991-92 and has worried some observers with his plan to unhitch the litas currency from the dollar.
But after early statements saying he wanted to end the link as soon as possible he has adopted a more gradual approach.
The president is expected formally to nominate Vagnorius during the week after parliament's first sitting on November 25 and Landsbergis said the government could be formed in around two weeks.
